london.name: London System
london.summary: An easy setup to remember: you play nearly the same moves almost every time, whatever your opponent does.

sicilian-l01.summary: Imbalance and the fight for d4

sicilian-l01-s01.text: With ...c5 you don't copy White: you fight for the d4 square from the side.

sicilian-l01-s02.text: You trade your c-pawn for White's central pawn. After that, you have more pawns in the center and White has more on the queenside.

sicilian-l01-s05.prompt: What is ...a6 for in the Najdorf?
sicilian-l01-s05.explanation: It stops a white bishop or knight from reaching b5 and prepares the queenside advance.

dutch.name: Dutch Defense
dutch.summary: A fixed-scheme defense against 1.d4: choose the Classical, the Stonewall or the Leningrad and play with a clear plan.

dutch-l01.title: The Dutch Idea
dutch-l01.summary: Control e4 and attack on the kingside

dutch-l01-s01.text: The Dutch starts with ...f5. This pawn controls e4 and prepares an attack on the kingside. It is a fixed scheme defense: you know where your pieces are going.

dutch-l01-s02.text: There are three schemes: the Classical (...e6 and ...Be7), the Stonewall (...d5 and ...e6), and the Leningrad (...g6 and ...Bg7). All three control e4 and seek the attack.

dutch-l01-s03.prompt: Which square does the f5 pawn control?
dutch-l01-s03.explanation: The f5 pawn looks at e4. If White plays e4, you can capture with fxe4 or let it pass.
feedback: d4 is occupied by the white pawn.
c4 is far from the f5 pawn.

dutch-l01-s04.prompt: What is the risk of the Dutch?
dutch-l01-s04.explanation: By advancing the f pawn, castling becomes weaker. That is why you must take care of the king and choose the right time to attack.
feedback: The Dutch does not lose a pawn in the opening.
You can castle: in fact, it is part of the plan.

dutch-l01-s05.text: Summary: the Dutch is a fixed scheme defense. You choose a structure, control e4, and attack on the kingside. Take care of the king and do not change the plan without reason.

dutch-l05-s01.text: The Classical is the most solid Dutch. With ...e6, ...Be7 and ...O-O you prepare the break ...e5. Then you look for ...Qe8, ...Qh5 or ...Ne4 depending on how White responds.

notes: The f5 pawn controls e4.

The break: you open the center and look for the attack.

dutch-l05-s03.prompt: What does the Classical aim for with ...e5?
dutch-l05-s03.explanation: The break ...e5 opens the e-file and the diagonal of the bishop on e7. If White captures, your pieces reach the center.
options: Open the center and attack the king
feedback: Exchanging queens is not the goal: you want to attack.
There is no pawn on d5 in this structure.

dutch-l05-s04.hint: The e6 pawn can advance two squares: e5 is free.
dutch-l05-s04.success: Correct. ...e5 opens the center and gives life to your bishop on e7.

dutch-l05-s05.text: Summary: the Classical is solid and flexible. If the center opens, you attack; if it closes, you maneuver with ...Qe8, ...Bd7 and ...Rf7. The break ...e5 is the key moment.

dutch-l06.title: Stonewall: ...d5 and ...e6
dutch-l06.summary: The solid structure with the knight on e4

dutch-l06-s01.text: The Stonewall fixes the pawns on d5 and e6 and brings the knight to e4. It is a solid structure: you control the center and the attack goes through the kingside.

notes: The Dutch.
The Stonewall: pawn on d5 and control of e4.
Supports d5 and prepares ...e6.
Fixes the d5-e6 structure.
The bishop aims at h2.
The queen supports ...e5 and the attack.
King is safe and the f8 rook is ready.

dutch-l06-s03.prompt: Which square is most important for the black knight in the Stonewall?
dutch-l06-s03.explanation: The knight on e4 dominates the center and participates in the attack. The other two squares are on the edge and do nothing.
feedback: b4 is far from the attack.
h4 is an edge square: the knight loses strength.

dutch-l06-s04.hint: The black king is on e8 and the h8 rook is waiting. Castle short.
dutch-l06-s04.success: Correct. ...O-O puts the king safe and connects the rooks.

dutch-l06-s05.text: Summary: the Stonewall is solid. d5 and e6 control the center, and the knight on e4 is a strong piece. The attack goes through the kingside, with ...Bd6, ...Qe7 and ...Rf7.

dutch-l07-s01.text: The Leningrad places the bishop on g7 and seeks the ...e5 break. It is the most dynamic Dutch: if the center opens, your pieces arrive quickly and the bishop on g7 pressures the queenside.

d6 is the square of the Stonewall.

dutch-l07-s04.success: Correct. ...e5 opens the center and the bishop on g7 gets involved.

dutch-l07-s05.text: Summary: the Leningrad is the most dynamic Dutch. The bishop on g7 and the ...e5 break open the center and attack. If the White center closes, maneuver with ...Qe8 and ...Rf7.

dutch-l08.title: Against 2.e4: The Staunton Gambit
dutch-l08.summary: Accept the pawn or return it

dutch-l08-s01.text: If White plays 2.e4, you enter the Staunton Gambit. White gives a pawn in the center; you can take the pawn or return it with ...d5 to complete development.

Return the pawn to open the center and develop.

dutch-l08-s03.explanation: The Staunton Gambit sacrifices a pawn to open the center and attack quickly. In return, White is down a pawn if they don't recover it.
feedback: d4 is already defended by the pawn on c3 and the queen.
Exchanging queens is not the goal of the gambit.

dutch-l08-s04.prompt: Return the pawn to open the center and develop.
dutch-l08-s04.hint: The pawn on d7 can advance two squares: d6 and d5 are free.
dutch-l08-s04.success: Correct. ...d5 returns the pawn, opens the center, and gives your pieces play.

dutch-l08-s05.text: Summary: against 2.e4, the Staunton Gambit. Accept the pawn and defend it with ...d5, or return it to complete development. The important thing is not to leave the king exposed.
